submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective detector with two narrow jobs: (a) it fires on verse-presenting or verse-analyzing text — the words lyrics/lyric/poem(s)/sonnet/verse, a poet-songwriter surname completing a full name, or a colon-plus-blank-line — only when the context presents, quotes, or structurally analyzes verse (published poems, lyric sheets, a labeled verse followed by a quoted line, discussion of a sonnet's turn); and (b) it fires on short fixed alphanumeric literals in formal syntax — a sha384/sha512 digest fragment inside an integrity attribute or a single short exponent/limit term (x^2, n^{-1}) in math/HTML markup. It stays weak or inactive for a bare indefinite 'a poem' in a school-task sentence, a musician name in non-verse recording-studio prose, long compositional sum-plus-fraction identities, and the same digest/formula strings in plain prose.
